file_role: 11_dependency_assumptions — the assumption index. Every inference that goes beyond explicit chart structure carries one of these indices. An assumption is a declared, labelled bridge with its chart basis attached (law 6); it is never evidence (authority tier 4).

assumption_index.statement: The day stem stands for the subject (the brand and the person running it); the hour stem stands for the matter at hand (the campaign / the content programme).
assumption_index.basis: standard QMDJ subject/matter binding; the chart supplies day 辛亥 and hour 丁酉 as explicit fields (E007, E008).
assumption_index.guard: If a different binding is used, the subject claims (C012) must be re-derived; the structural claims do not depend on it.

assumption_index.statement: Gate and deity offices map to media behaviour classes, not to named platforms. The mapping table is declared below.
assumption_index.basis: annex A-patterns gate register (classical office of each gate); the chart supplies the gates.
assumption_index.guard: The chart names no platform and never can; any platform name in the deliverable is an illustration inside this assumption, not a chart finding.

assumption_index.statement: Gate/star offices map to content functions used to derive pillars (teaching, display, quiet proof, alliance, restraint).
assumption_index.basis: annex A-patterns gate register + star offices as used in the marker register.
assumption_index.guard: Pillars are labelled by function first and by example second; the example is the assignment's own worked archetype (A-007).

assumption_index.statement: Gate offices map to KPI classes: opening -> entry metrics, view/display -> reach, hidden support -> private accumulation (saves), generation -> value metrics, alliance -> collaboration count, rest -> comment quality.
assumption_index.guard: No metric values or benchmarks are supplied; only the metric class and the objective it serves.

assumption_index.statement: Deity offices map to creator classes: hidden support -> nano/micro educators, alliance -> micro partners, radiance/highest -> macro, contest -> controversy-driving creators (excluded).
assumption_index.guard: No creator is named from the chart; creator identity is an unresolved unknown (UNK01-UNK04 block), delivered as a rubric plus two slots.

assumption_index.statement: The two selected primary objectives (awareness through display; education through the governing star) are read from the two most heavily marked favourable palaces rather than from the whole field.
assumption_index.basis: palace 1 (E005, E006, E012, E022) and palace 8 (E085, E086, E095).
assumption_index.guard: Community and conversion are explicitly not selected as primary; their chart support and their limits are recorded in the alignment ledger.

assumption_index.statement: Where an example is needed, the deliverable uses the worked example supplied inside the assignment document itself (a better-for-you snack context: 'Snack Smarter', '4 PM office hunger'). It is labelled SOURCE_EXAMPLE and is not a chart finding and not a statement about the student's brand.
assumption_index.guard: Every illustrated row carries a substitution slot so the student's own brand from Assignment 1 replaces it without touching the strategy.

assumption_index.statement: The 25-batch coverage protocol is derived from the charter's own protocol section and B3 topic list because annex A-coverage was not supplied.
assumption_index.basis: charter law 29 + protocol B0-B5/P6/RT + B3 topic enumeration.
assumption_index.guard: Batch count and topic order are listed explicitly so a supplied annex can be diffed against them.

assumption_index.statement: The pattern catalog and archetype rubric are the sanctioned minimum-viable stand-in declared in CONFIG/marker_reference.json: three pattern classes (stem combination, gate reconciliation, structural marker) and four archetype families (concentration, visibility, private gain, friction).
assumption_index.basis: charter annex A-patterns / A-archetypes permission to port a minimum viable stand-in.
assumption_index.guard: Every archetype label in the package lists its competing candidates and its rejection reasons, so a supplied rubric can re-rank them.

assumption_index.statement: The seven analysed facets are ranked by DECISION_RELEVANCE against the brief's own evaluation criteria (AMEND-01 supersedes the v1 SOURCE_DEPENDENCY_ORDER fallback); the remaining four are registered as deferred.
assumption_index.basis: CONFIG/context_amendment.json -> facet_ranking; the source supplies 11 facets and its 4 evaluation criteria select 7.
assumption_index.guard: Deferral is recorded per facet with its claim count and tag tally; if the operator promotes an execution facet, the criterion must be re-applied and the deferral list rewritten.

assumption_index.statement: The structural subject statement (C012) is retained with an explicit uncertainty marker and does not assert anything about the real persona; the persona remains UNK02.
assumption_index.guard: Any text that would describe the persona is replaced by a slot; the delivery notes flag this explicitly.

assumption_index.statement: Call cost is measured as the whitespace-token count of each capability's printed summary; the cap's max_out_tokens is enforced against that count.
assumption_index.basis: no tokenizer is available in this runtime; the metric is declared in CONFIG/run_config.json.
assumption_index.guard: Costs are reproducible: the same summary text yields the same count.

assumption_index.statement: AMEND-01 records the operator's declaration that the assignment brief is the case context and the reason the chart was cast. It re-classifies the ingestion path to free_prose and fills the six case-context slots; every filled row stays tagged DECOMPOSED.
assumption_index.guard: The v1 CONTEXT_DEGRADED stamp is retained in the package; no derived row acquires veto power; no chart-layer product may change on account of this amendment (cc1/cc2).
